Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:11:1.english: Bei dappa - An olive press for oil.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:12:1.hebrew: לפופי - אמולידי"ר בלע"ז, לשון מלפפין הוולד (שבת דף קכט:), שמגלגלו לפי מדתו — אם גדולות, אם קטנות — ועושה להן בית קיבול:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:12:1.english: Rolling - Amoledir [to shape/mold] in Old French, [from] the expression "they swaddle [melapefin] the newborn" (Shabbat 129b), for he rolls it according to its measure — whether large or small — and makes a receptacle for them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:12:2.english: And burning - To fire it in the kiln.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:12:3.hebrew: כגון דמלפף ויבש - ואכתי ביצים קרי להו, לשון ביצה — מרשק"א — שהעפר מגובלת עם המים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:12:3.english: Where they were rolled and dried - And still [the Mishnah] calls them "beitzim" — [from] the word "bitzah" (marsh; Old French: maresc), because the earth is kneaded with water.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:13:1.hebrew: ומידק - לאחר שנשרפו האבנים, הרי הן חתיכות שרופות, ומוציאין אותן מן הכבשן, ונותנין בהן מעט מים, וצוברין אותן, ונידוכות מאליהן כקמח טחון:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:13:1.english: And grinding - After the stones have been burned, they are burnt pieces; and they take them out of the kiln, put a little water on them, and pile them up, and they crumble on their own like ground flour.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:13:2.hebrew: משראוי לשקען בכבשן - משהכין והזמין את האבנים ואת העצים, והכל בידו, ואין חסר אלא מלאכת השריפה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:13:2.english: From when it is fit to sink them in the kiln - Once he has prepared and readied the stones and the wood, and everything is in his hands, and nothing is lacking except the work of burning.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:14:1.hebrew: בד"א - שצריך שיהא מוכן בידו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:14:1.english: In what [case] is this statement said - That it must be ready in his hand.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:14:2.hebrew: בעפר לבן - שאינו מצוי, וכשהיו מכניסין אותו, אין מכניסין אותו אלא מגובל ועשוי ביצים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:14:2.english: With white earth - For it is not common, and when they would bring it in, they would only bring it in kneaded and made into egg-shaped clumps.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:14:3.hebrew: אבל בעפר שחור - שהוא מצוי במקומו, אין צריך שיהא בידו, שאם אין לזה יש לזה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:14:3.english: But regarding black earth - Since it is readily available in its place, it does not need to be in his possession, for if this one does not have [it], that one has [it].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:15:1.hebrew: מכי עיילי עפרא - משהכניס המוכר וצבר עפר בביתו, ועפר שחור היה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:15:1.english: From when they bring in the earth - From [the time] when the seller brought in and piled up earth in his house, and it was black earth.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:15:2.english: Earth was scarce - [It was] rare and not commonly found.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:15:3.hebrew: סמכא דעתיה - דכל אחד, והחוזר יקבל מי שפרע:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:15:3.english: His mind relied [on it] - [That is, the mind] of each one [of them relies on the transaction], and the one who retracts will receive [the curse of] "He who punished" [mi shepara].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:15:4.hebrew: לא סמכא דעתיה - דלמא לא משכח עפרא, וליכא מי שפרע, שהוא עצמו לא נסמך עליו, אלא נתן על הספק:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:15:4.english: He did not rely [on it] - [Because] perhaps [the seller] will not find earth, and there is no [imprecation of] "He who exacted punishment" [mi shepara], since he himself did not rely on him, rather he gave [the money] in uncertainty.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:1:1.english: Not in his power - Perhaps they will not sell it to him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:2:1.english: That he did not wrap and seal - the money of each and every person separately.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:3:1.hebrew: סיטומתא - חותם שרושמין החנונים על החביות של יין שלוקחין הרבה ביחד, ומניחין אותו באוצר הבעלים, ומוליכין אותן אחת אחת למכור לחנות, ורושמין אותם לדעת שכל הרשומות נמכרות:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:3:1.english: Situmta - A mark that shopkeepers imprint on barrels of wine that they buy many [of] together, and they leave it in the owner's storehouse and take them one by one to sell at the shop; and they mark them so that it is known that all the marked [barrels] are sold.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:5:1.hebrew: ובאתרא כו' למיקני - שרגילין לרשום על מנת שבדבר זה תהא קנויה לו כאלו משך, קני:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:5:1.english: And in a place, etc., to acquire - Where they are accustomed to mark [the item] on condition that through this act it shall be acquired by him as if he had pulled [it], [he] acquires [it].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:7:1.hebrew: פוסק עמו - ואע"פ שלא יצא השער, דהא יש לו; אבל מחוסר שלש, כאין לו דמי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:7:1.english: He may set [a price] with him - Even though the market price has not [yet] come out, for he has it; but [that which is] lacking three [actions] is like not having it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:7:2.english: Placing [it] in the sun - Spreading out the sheaves in the sun.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:7:3.english: And winnowing - To throw the chaff after threshing with a winnowing shovel in the wind.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:7:4.english: Where he placed [it] in the sun and it dried - For it is still called a stack [of grain].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:8:1.hebrew: בידי אדם - אם מלאכות שהדבר מחוסר בידי אדם, אפי' מאה הן, פוסק:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:8:1.english: By the hand of man - If the tasks that the item is lacking [are] by the hand of man, even [if] they are a hundred, he may set [a price].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:8:2.hebrew: בידי שמים אפי' אחת אינו פוסק - דמי יימר דאתיא ויהא בידו להשלים, הלכך כאין לו הוא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:8:2.english: [If it is] by the hand of Heaven, he may not set [a price for] even one - For who can say that it will come and it will be in his power to complete [it]? Therefore, it is as though he does not have [it].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:8:3.hebrew: האיכא מידרא - דבידי שמים היא, שצריך רוח שאינה מצויה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:8:3.english: Isn't there winnowing - which is in the hands of Heaven, for it requires wind, which is not [always] readily available.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:8:4.hebrew: אפשר בנפוותא - וו"ן בלע"ז:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:8:4.english: It is possible with sieves - Van in Old French [a winnowing fan].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:9:1.english: For the basket - [The Gemara] proceeds to cite all of them in order to challenge Rav and Shmuel.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:9:3.english: To tread - To tread in the winepress.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:9:4.english: Drawing - To draw the wine into the pit in front of the winepress.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:9:5.english: As Rabbi Ḥiyya teaches - Later [in the Gemara].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:9:6.hebrew: על הכומר של זיתים - דתנן במתניתין (לעיל בבא מציעא דף עב:) מעטן, תנא ליה איהו במתני' בלשון כומר, לומר שכבר נתחממו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 74a:9:6.english: For a stack [komer] of olives - That which we learned in our Mishnah (above, Bava Metzia 72b) [as] ma'atan, he [Rabbi Ḥiyya] taught in [his] baraita using the term komer, to indicate that they have already been warmed.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 74a:11:1.hebrew: תני רבי חייא על כומר של זיתים - וא"ת: אמאי לא אמר רבי חייא מילתיה ארישא, דעביט של ענבים? ויש לומר: דאין רגילות למכמר ענבים כמו זיתים. וא"ת: לשמואל, דאמר בידי אדם אפילו מאה פוסק, למה לי "על כומר"? ויש לומר: דכימור הזיתים מקרי בידי שמים:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 74a:11:1.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya teaches: "For a stack of olives" - And if you will say: Why did Rabbi Ḥiyya not state his teaching regarding the first clause, of a vat of grapes? And one can say that it is not customary to warm grapes [in a stack] like olives. And if you will say: According to Shmuel, who said [that if the lacking actions are] in human hands, even [if there are] a hundred, one may set a price — why do I need [the reading] "for a stack [of olives]"? And one can say that the warming of olives is considered [to be] in the hands of Heaven:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 74a:14:1.hebrew: וכפר שיחין וחברותיה אע"פ שאין לזה יש לזה - לא מיירי בעפרא, דהא מחוסר שלש הוא ואינו פוסק, אלא בביצים איירי. ומדנקט האי לישנא דאע"פ שאין לזה יש לזה, כדנקט גבי "פוסקין על שער שבשוק", משמע שיש שער שבשוק לביצים. וקמ"ל דאע"פ שאין שער לקדירות שבשוק, כיון שיש שער לביצים — חשיב כאילו יש לו ביצים, לפסוק לקדירות כשער מוכרי קדירות בזול; שהביצים לענין קדירות כעין לקוטות למוכרי תבואה. אי נמי: אפילו אין שער, יכול להיות דחשיב כיש לו, לפי שדרך יוצרים דיזפי מהדדי, שיש הרבה מהם:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 74a:14:1.english: And Kefar Shiḥin and its environs, even if this one does not [have it], that one has [it] - It is not speaking of [raw] earth, for that lacks three [stages of preparation] and one cannot set a price [on it]; rather, it is speaking of clumps of clay. And since it uses this wording, "even if this one does not [have it], that one has [it]," just as it uses [in the Mishnah] regarding "one may set a price at the market rate," it implies that there is a market rate for clumps of clay. And it teaches us that even though there is no market rate for pots in the market, since there is a market rate for clumps of clay, it is considered as though he has clumps of clay, [allowing him] to set a price for pots at the low rate of pot sellers; for clumps of clay with respect to pots are like gleanings for grain sellers. Alternatively: even if there is no market rate, it could be that it is considered as though he has [them], because it is the practice of potters to borrow from one another, as there are many of them.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 74a:1:1.hebrew: הכא לאו בידו - מכאן מקשה ר"ת לפירוש הקונט' דפרק זה בורר (סנהדרין דף כד: ושם ד"ה כל), גבי משחק בקוביא, דקאמר התם דלאו אסמכתא היא. ופי' הקונט': משום דהיכי דמי אסמכתא? כגון "אם אוביר ולא אעביד", וכגון משליש שטרו דגט פשוט (ב"ב דף קסח. ושם) — דסמיך על (לא) דבר, כסבור כל זה בידו לעשות, ומרישא כי מתני, אדעתא דלא יהיב לאסמכתא קא מתני, דטועה שלא יבא לידי כך; אבל משחק בקוביא לא סמיך אמידי, דלא ידע אי נצח אי לא נצח, ואפ"ה מתני — שמע מינה מספיקא גמיר ומקני! והכא משמע איפכא, דהיכא דלאו בידו הוי טפי אסמכתא. ונראה לר"ת דהתם משום הכי לא הוי אסמכתא, דאגב דבעי למיקני גמר ומקני. וקשה לפירושו, דבהזהב (לעיל בבא מציעא דף מח: ושם) חשיב אסמכתא לההיא ד"אם אני חוזר בי ערבוני מחול לך", ולא אמרי' מגו דבעי למיקני גמר ומקני; ועוד, דא"כ היכי מדמה בפרק זה בורר (סנהדרין דף כה.) לההיא ד"אין אחד מהם נזיר", דהתם לא שייך האי טעמא! ור"ת בעצמו חזר בו, והגיה בספר הישר גבי עובדא דשנים שהמרו זה את זה בפרק במה מדליקין (שבת דף לא.) שהקנו זה לזה, דאי לא הקנו ליהדרו בהו. ואע"ג דיש מקומות דקנו בלא קנין בדברים בעלמא, כגון בסנהדרין (דף כד.): "נאמן עלי אבא" כו', דבאתן לך מחלוקת, וכן (שם): "דור לי בחיי ראשך" דאין יכול לחזור בו — התם דין הוא שיועיל, כיון שיש להם תביעה זה על זה והם קבלו עליהם כך את הדין, ולא דמי להיכא שאין לו שום תביעה. והתם בפ' זה בורר (סנהדרין דף כה.) גבי מפריחי יונים משמע כפי' הקונט', דקאמר "וצריכא" — דאי קאמר בתולה בדעת עצמו, התם דקאמר "קים לי בנפשאי דידענא טפי", ולהכי הוי אסמכתא; משמע היכא דבידו להרויח הויא טפי אסמכתא. ומהך דשמעתין נראה לי דלא דמי, דהכא הויא בידו ולא בידו, דאע"ג דמצוי הוא לקנות, מכל מקום כיון דתלוי באחרים — דאם לא ירצו למכור, ממי יקנה — הלכך לא גמר ומקני; אבל התם דאין בידו כלל, גמר ומקני. וכשהיה בידו מכל וכל, כגון "אם אוביר ולא אעביד", אי גזים לא גמר ומקני, כגון דאמר "אשלם אלפא זוזי", כדלקמן בפרק המקבל (בבא מציעא דף קד:); אבל "אשלם במיטבא" דלא גזים, גמר ומקני. ועוד פר"ת: דוקא כי ההיא ד"אם אני חוזר בי ערבוני מחול לך", וההיא דפירקין לעיל (בבא מציעא דף סה:) ד"אם אי אתה נותן לי מכאן ועד שלש שנים", וההיא דמשליש חשיב אסמכתא, כיון דגזים — שאין מתכוין אלא להסמיך חברו על דבריו שיאמינהו; אבל משחק בקוביא אדעתא דהכי קא עבדי שירויחו זה או זה. ובסנהדרין [דף כד: ד"ה כל] האריך בפסק משחק בקוביא:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 74a:1:1.english: Here, [it is] not in his power - From here Rabbeinu Tam raises a difficulty against Rashi's explanation in the chapter [entitled] Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 24b, and there, s.v. Kol) regarding a dice player, where [the Gemara] says there that it is not an asmakhta. And Rashi explained: Because what is a case of asmakhta? Such as "If I leave [the field] fallow and do not work [it]," and such as one who deposits his document with a third party in [the chapter entitled] Get Pashut (Bava Batra 168a, and there) — where he relies on something, thinking all of this is in his power to do, and from the outset when he stipulates, he stipulates with the intention that he will not [actually] give [it], as an asmakhta, for he mistakenly thinks he will not come to such a pass. However, a dice player does not rely on anything, for he does not know whether he will win or not win, and even so he stipulates — infer from this that despite the uncertainty, he fully resolves and transfers [the money]. Yet here [the Gemara] implies the opposite, that where it is not in his power, it is more [considered] an asmakhta! And it appears to Rabbeinu Tam that there, for this reason it is not an asmakhta: because in his desire to acquire [the other's stake], he fully resolves and transfers [his own]. Yet [this] is difficult according to his explanation, for in [the chapter entitled] HaZahav (above, Bava Metzia 48b, and there), [the Gemara] considers as an asmakhta that [case] of "If I retract, my deposit is forfeited to you," and we do not say "since he wants to acquire, he fully resolves and transfers"! And furthermore, if so, how does [the Gemara] compare [it] in the chapter [entitled] Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 25a) to that [case] of "neither of them is a Nazirite," for there this reason does not apply! And Rabbeinu Tam himself retracted, and emended [it] in Sefer HaYashar regarding the incident of two people who wagered with one another in the chapter [entitled] Bameh Madlikin (Shabbat 31a), [explaining] that they made a formal act of acquisition (kinyan) with one another, for had they not made a kinyan, they could have retracted. And even though there are places where they acquire without a kinyan, through mere words — such as in Sanhedrin (24a): "My father is trustworthy to me," etc., where [the case is] "in 'I will give you'" [there is a] dispute, and similarly (there): "Vow to me by the life of your head," where he cannot retract — there it is logical that it should be effective, since they have a [pre-existing] claim against one another and they accepted the judgment upon themselves in this manner, and it is not comparable to [a case] where he has no claim whatsoever. And there in the chapter [entitled] Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 25a) regarding pigeon racers, it implies like Rashi's explanation, for [the Gemara] says, "And it is necessary" — for if it had [only] stated [the case of] one who relies on his own judgment, there [it is] because he says, "I am certain of myself that I know better," and therefore it is an asmakhta; [this] implies that where it is in his power to profit, it is more [considered] an asmakhta. And from this [passage] in our Gemara, it appears to me that it is not comparable: for here it is [both] in his power and not in his power, since even though it is common to buy [wine], nevertheless since it depends on others — for if they do not wish to sell, from whom will he buy? — therefore he does not fully resolve and transfer; whereas there, where it is not in his power at all, he does fully resolve and transfer. And when it is completely in his power, such as "If I leave [the field] fallow and do not work [it]," if he exaggerates he does not fully resolve and transfer — such as where he says "I will pay a thousand zuz," as [stated] below in the chapter [entitled] HaMekabel (Bava Metzia 104b); but [if he says] "I will pay with the best [produce]," where he does not exaggerate, he fully resolves and transfers. And furthermore Rabbeinu Tam explained: Specifically like that [case] of "If I retract, my deposit is forfeited to you," and that [case] in our chapter above (Bava Metzia 65b) of "If you do not pay me between now and three years," and that [case] of one who deposits [his document] with a third party, is considered an asmakhta, since he exaggerates — for he intends only to make his fellow rely on his words so that he will trust him; however, a dice player — they act with this intention, that either this one or that one will profit. And in Sanhedrin [24b, s.v. Kol], he elaborated on the ruling regarding a dice player.
